title: At the Kings' Gate
journal: The Eye of Argonia is the old priest-kings' jewel. It sits at the Root, under the sea below Teku-Sul Spire, where the roots of every Hist meet; used there, it can heal every sick tree. The last king shut it behind the Kings' Gate, which opens only with three seal-stones. I carry all three seal-stones of the kings' gate. I'm to bring them to Never-Writes-Twice, who stands at the back of Nesh-Deeka's House in Helstrom.
objectives: Bring the three seal-stones to Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka's House, Helstrom. (marker: Never-Writes-Twice)

plan.going: The Eye of Argonia, the old kings' jewel, sits at the Root under Teku-Sul, where the roots of every Hist meet; used there it heals every sick tree. The Kings' Gate shuts it in and opens only with three seal-stones. I have all three stones the ghost at Teku-Sul named; the order wants them
plan.next: report to Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka's House, Helstrom
plan.ways: none; the report is the step

answers: I carry three seal-stones that open the Kings' Gate, which guards the Eye of Argonia under the sea below Teku-Sul Spire. The Eye can heal the sick Hist trees. A rival, the Collector Ennodius Vanin, is also after it.
Bring the three stones to Never-Writes-Twice at the back of Nesh-Deeka's House in Helstrom.
I can go straight to Never-Writes-Twice and hand over the stones, or talk first to ask questions. I have not yet seen other choices.
I do not understand why the Unbound seal trees, what moans in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar, or how Nesh-Deeka knows of the Unbound. I could ask Never-Writes-Twice.

title: At the Kings' Gate
journal: Never-Writes-Twice made me a Ka-Deelith, a War-Teacher of the Toh-Reel-Ka, and gave me the order's pike. Her watchers have not seen the Unbound near Teku-Sul, so I am ahead of them. I'm to dive to Teku-Sul Spire, open the Kings' Gate with the three stones and use the Eye where it sits to heal the trees. Then I'm to bring the stones back to her and hunt down Cuts-the-Old-Knot.
objectives: Dive to Teku-Sul Spire and go to the Kings' Gate. (marker: The Kings' Gate)

plan.going: I am a Ka-Deelith now. The order thinks I am ahead of the Unbound and has sent me to open the gate and heal the trees with the Eye; afterwards the stones go back to Never-Writes-Twice and I hunt Cuts-the-Old-Knot
plan.next: dive to Teku-Sul and go to the Kings' Gate
plan.ways: carry waterbreathing for the dive; in the east halls Unbound I was not warned of wait for me: fight them, slip past or hold them off with magic

answers: Never-Writes-Twice made me Ka-Deelith of the Toh-Reel-Ka and gave me a pike and armour. The Unbound are not yet near Teku-Sul, so I am ahead of them.

Dive to Teku-Sul Spire and go to the Kings' Gate, set the three stones, and use the Eye where it sits to heal the trees without lifting it. Then take the stones back to her and hunt Cuts-the-Old-Knot.
I can go to the gate now; later I decide how to deal with the Eye. I have been told not to lift it.
I do not know why the Unbound seal trees, what is in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar, or how Nesh-Deeka knows the Unbound. I could ask Never-Writes-Twice.

title: At the Kings' Gate
journal: Cuts-the-Old-Knot was waiting before the Kings' Gate, without stones. She says the Toh-Reel-Ka keep dreamers in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth, fed on sap, and see the whole marsh through them. She was one of them for nine years, and Never-Writes-Twice kept the key. That is why she seals the trees she drains: a sealed tree shows the dreamers nothing. If I fight her, I take what she carries and go on alone, and giving her the Eye is closed to me. If I believe her, she fights the guardian beside me. Either way the choice at the Eye stays mine. Used where it sits, the Eye heals every tree, and the dreamers see through them all again; lifted, it parts the trees, about three in ten die, and the dreams end. I'm to choose.
objectives: Fight Cuts-the-Old-Knot, or believe her. (marker: Cuts-the-Old-Knot)

plan.going: Cuts-the-Old-Knot told me what the Toh-Reel-Ka are: they see the marsh through sap-fed dreamers in Fort Chalkmoth's cellar, the moaning I heard. She seals trees to blind them, not to kill the trees. The healing I was sent to do would let the dreamers see again, and the stones in the order's hands would keep the Eye theirs. She wants the Eye lifted, which ends the dreams and kills many trees. This answers the question in my journal. Used where it sits, the Eye heals every tree and lets the dreamers see through them all; lifted, it parts the trees for good, about three in ten die, and the dreams end
plan.next: choose whether to fight her or believe her
plan.ways: fight: the hardest fight yet (she drinks her draught and fights as a battlemage); I get her spell tomes, robes, staff and draughts; I face the guardian alone; at the Eye I can only use it or take it. Believe: she waits in the hall beyond the gate and fights the guardian beside me; at the Eye I can use it, take it, or give it to her. Using the Eye with her alive kills her

answers: Cuts-the-Old-Knot waits at the Kings' Gate. She says the Toh-Reel-Ka keep sap-fed dreamers in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar to watch the marsh through the trees, that she was one, and that Never-Writes-Twice lied. She seals trees so the dreamers cannot see. Using the Eye in place heals all trees but keeps the dreams; lifting it ends the dreams and kills about three in ten trees.
Choose here: fight her or believe her.
Fight her and go on alone, or believe her so she fights the guardian beside me. The final choice at the Eye stays mine either way.
I cannot verify her claims, and I do not know what the guardian is. I could learn more at the gate.

title: At the Kings' Gate
journal: I chose to believe Cuts-the-Old-Knot. She will wait in the hall beyond the gate and fight the guardian with me. I have not promised her the Eye. I'm to set the three stones in the Kings' Gate.

plan.going: I chose to believe Cuts-the-Old-Knot. She will wait in the hall beyond the gate and fight the guardian with me. I have not promised her the Eye. I'm to set the three stones in the Kings' Gate.
plan.next: nothing more in this quest; the next quests entry carries the step

answers: I chose to believe Cuts-the-Old-Knot over Never-Writes-Twice. She will fight the guardian beside me beyond the gate. I have promised her nothing about the Eye.
Set the three seal-stones in the Kings' Gate at the sunken ruin.
After the gate, I decide at the Eye whether to use it in place (heals all trees, dreams continue) or lift it (ends the dreams, about three in ten trees die). I would still need to weigh both.
I do not know what the guardian is, and I cannot confirm whether the dreamer story is true. I could check the Fort Chalkmoth cellar.
